News.title: The squad of motorbike-riding women fighting wildfires in the jungle
News.content:
Indonesia’s fires are bad. Siti Nuriani knows this. Seven years ago, a terrible haze suffocated her village in Kalimantan, the southern, Indonesian part of the island of Borneo.

The acrid smoke travelled through the air. It flowed into houses, and wended its way into people’s lungs. For some, things took a frightening turn. The toxic particles exacerbated respiratory diseases: asthma, chronic bronchitis; increased heart problems and cases of cancer.

Siti’s son, then 14, was admitted to hospital with severe asthma. Luckily, he survived, but many didn’t. There were more than 87,000 excess deaths in Indonesia in 2019 due to exposure to the haze, according to one study.

Now, there are fears another monster fire is about to hit Indonesia. The UN has warned the world to prepare for a Super El Nino which could trigger extreme weather – for example, heavy rainfall in the American south, or drought in sub Saharan Africa – and a shorter rainy season in Indonesia this year and next.

The dry season in Indonesia typically lasts from July to October. But the weather has been unusually dry this March and April.

This is a worry because of Indonesia’s highly combustible land. Tropical peatland covers 20.6m hectares or just over 10 per cent of the country. Peatland is usually too wet to burn, but not in Indonesia where it is cleared and drained and dried to grow crops, such as oil palms which make people rich. Slash-and-burn agriculture is a common catalyst of wildfires.

“People don’t realise tropical peatlands are a big feature of our tropics and when those fires get going they’re impossible to put out and they have in the past created a horrible smoke haze over the whole of South East Asia,” said Professor Myles Allen, head of atmospheric, oceanic and planetary physics at the University of Oxford. They also put a lot of carbon in the atmosphere, he added, “which doesn’t help us either”.

News.title: Global stocks plunge in AI ‘bloodbath’
News.content:
Chipmaker Kioxia collapsed 16pc, meaning it has lost around half its value since briefly overtaking Toyota to become Japan’s biggest listed company last month.

Taiwan’s Taiex index had shed 6.5pc after $2tn chip giant TSMC fell by 7.3pc a day after announcing record second-quarter profit but higher than expected spending plans.

European stocks also fell, while Wall Street was on track to suffer a further drop at the opening bell. The Nasdaq 100 slumped 2pc in premarket trading on Friday, a day after Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company, suffered a 2.4pc drop.

It has also been a bruising week for semiconductor companies in the US, which have risen sharply so far this year.

Micron fell 5.6pc on Thursday, although it remained 199pc higher than at the start of the year. Memory chip company SanDisk fell 12.6pc, although it remained up 494pc for the year. Western Digital sank 9.2pc but was still up 171pc for the year.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “Global equities are continuing to slump, as fresh doubts about the AI trade have driven a pronounced sell-off in tech stocks.”

Mr Reid said there had been no single trigger for the downturn, which came as the world’s biggest technology companies prepared to report their second quarter results.

Markets have come under pressure from the renewed hostilities in the Middle East, which have sent oil prices soaring more than 15pc this month to over $85 a barrel.

Kevin Warsh, the new chairman of the Federal Reserve, insisted that he would seek to keep a lid on inflation during testimony in front of Congress this week. Many traders took his remarks as a warning that interest rates could remain elevated in the coming months.

Others suggested the mood has been dampened by SpaceX, which has fallen 35pc from its record highs set days after its blockbuster float in June. It is now trading below its listing price of $135 per share.

However, the FTSE 100 bucked the trend on Friday, rising by 0.5pc in early trading. It has lower exposure to the technology sector than other European markets.

Johan Javeus, senior economist at SEB, said: “The sell-off is partly driven by profit-taking on many AI stocks, coupled with the recurring doubts of an AI investment bubble.

“The fact that the SpaceX IPO has done so poorly makes many investors extra nervous.”

News.title: McIlroy loses his touch as DeChambeau mocks Faldo
News.content:
So, England are out of the World Cup and all hopes of ending those 60 years’ of hurt have been well and truly bunkered once again. Would an English winner of the Claret Jug make up for the footballers’ early demise against Argentina? Nope? Didn’t think so, but there are several home hopes who head into the four days at Royal Birkdale with decent chances of becoming the Champion Golfer of the Year.

Among them is Justin Rose who first came to prominence as a fresh-faced 17-year-old at Birkdale in 1998, when, as an amateur he finished tied-fourth having been in contention to win. Should the world No 10 get his hands on golf’s most-famous trophy at the course he first made his name it would be a victory that few, if any, would begrudge him. He’s waited over a decade to win a second major and the feeling is that as he gets older the Open is the tournament that offers him the best chance of doing that.

Then there is local boy Tommy Fleetwood. The 35-year-old is from Southport, a lob wedge from Birkdale’s first tee, and a victory for the world No 9, in what would be his first (long-awaited) major, would also be a popular one.

As for the big names, Rory McIlroy comes in in good form after impressing at the Scottish Open without ever seemingly getting close to fifth gear and world No 1 Scottie Scheffler tees it up on the back of a first missed cut in nearly four years (a run of 78 cuts made ended).

The other big talking point is the weather. No one can remember the last time they saw a a cloud in the sky let alone rain and the fairways are brown, hard and will provide a ‘true’ links summer test: think Hoylake in 2006 rather than Carnoustie 1999.

Stay here for all the action on day one as we take you from the early tee times right through until the final putt drops at around 9pm.

News.title: Brilliant Root picks off India to set up decider
News.content:
At some point England will face the very uncomfortable feeling of life without Joe Root. He will turn 36 this year and even his powers will wane one day.

At the moment there is no sign of it happening and with 99 not out from 133 balls, he led England to a series-levelling four wicket win in Cardiff which was not pretty but potentially an important step in the development of this team if the others can learn from the master Root.

“Just get it done,” he said to Gus Atkinson when stuck at the non-striker’s end one short of his hundred and England requiring just three to win with more than five overs to bowl. Atkinson obliged, pulling Prasidh Krishna for four but it was Root who was serenaded off the ground with the Barmy Army rendition of his name set to Hey Jude.

News.title: ‘I feel like I’m in front of a fireball’: 45C heat becomes India’s new normal
News.content:
Even under the shade of an umbrella, the fierce heat is unbearable. It’s nearing midday as Gulab Padiyar hammers yet another metal sheet into a simple bucket, but temperatures topped 40C hours ago.

“I feel like I’m in front of a gas stove – or a fireball,” Ms Padiyar says, perched on a once-white cushion beside a dusty road. “I feel like I’m cooking myself.”

The 53-year-old has little choice: it’s heat or hunger. Each day, Ms Padiyar earns around 400 rupees (roughly £3) making dozens of buckets – it’s just enough for her and her husband to survive.

“I feel dizzy and my eyes burn, sometimes I get headaches or faint,” she says. “But at the end of the day… this is the work I know, and others won’t employ me because of my age. So I think I have to continue, no matter how hot it gets.”

Ms Padiyar’s hometown, Ahmedabad, is no stranger to scorching temperatures. Home to roughly 8.5 million people, it’s the largest city in Gujarat – an arid state in western India where both Mahatma Gandhi and Narendra Modi, the country’s Prime Minister, were born.

But the mercury is rising. In the 1990s, the hot season between mid-March and mid-June averaged roughly 35 days above 40C, according to analysis from The Times of India. This year, that number hit 71. A study from the University of Oxford this month ranked Ahmedabad as the world’s second most “heat-risk city”, after Basra in Iraq.

Yet the Indian city has also been a trailblazer in extreme heat policy. Its experiences in the last 15 years offer strategies to adapt – and a warning about just how difficult that is, especially to protect workers in a “survival economy”.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola ‘had verbal AGREEMENT’ to be England manager before Three Lions turned to Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
FORMER Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola reportedly had a verbal agreement in place with England before Thomas Tuchel was appointed manager.

Guardiola was heavily linked with the England job when Gareth Southgate decided to step down two years ago.



He refused to rule the move out at the time but ultimately decided to renew his contract with City midway through the 2024/25 season.

The Athletic now reports that Guardiola actually had a verbal agreement in place with the FA before changing his mind.



The Spaniard’s change of heart resulted in FA chiefs recruiting Tuchel instead.

Tuchel was announced as the new England boss in October 2024 but did not officially start the job until the following January.

At the time, the main goal was to reach the World Cup final this summer.

However, the Three Lions crashed out in the last four.

England suffered a 2-1 semi-final defeat to Argentina on Wednesday.

And Tuchel faced heavy criticism for his tactical changes and substitutions in the second half.

After going 1-0 up against the reigning world champions, England stepped back and took a more defensive approach.

That invited a huge amount of pressure and they were punished by Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez as a result.

Some fans and pundits called for Tuchel to be sacked following the defeat.

But the manager insists he is fully committed to leading England into Euro 2028 – which is a home tournament.

He said: “One hundred per cent, and there’s still enough to improve, still enough to improve and I’m more than happy to do that.



“I still think we can impose ourselves more on the ball, I still think we can still show how good football players we are.

“I think it’s still in us because I see it in training in every camp and here also in the World Cup and I still feel there is an extra level that we need to conquer and we need to step up on the next level and then to get the big prize.”

Sports.title: Secret clause in Thomas Tuchel’s England contract revealed that could have seen him and FA agree to part ways
Sports.content:
THOMAS TUCHEL and the FA could have ended things after the World Cup due to a secret contract clause – but only if the Three Lions lost before the quarter-finals.

According to The Athletic, either party would have been able to initiate a split should England have crashed out early this summer.



Both sides would have been entitled to huge compensation should the other have backed out of their short-term relationship.

Tuchel has batted away interest from Manchester United since being appointed as England boss, for example, and is on massive pay for his role as an esteemed foreign head coach.



But everyone agreed to make an exemption when it emerged that England could come up against tournament co-hosts Mexico in their own back yard in the last-16.

Under the contract, a defeat in that game would have allowed either Tuchel or the FA to call it quits there and then.



Such was the challenge of playing an effective away game in the rowdy Azteca at altitude in that scenario, they agreed to waive it – and they shouldn’t have worried.

England managed one of their best ever results – winning 3-2 in Mexico City and securing a place in the quarter-finals.

But Tuchel has faced immense backlash this week despite going a step further and beating Norway in the next round.

His handling of the final 40 minutes in the semi against Argentina on Wednesday has left England fans furious.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

The German boss made defensive changes to try and see out a 1-0 win after Anthony Gordon‘s goal opened up a tight game.

And it backfired with an already retreating side dropping deeper and deeper.

England had just 12 per cent of the ball between Gordon’s goal and Lautaro Martinez heading in a winner for Argentina in stoppage time.

There was no way back, and many have lost it with Tuchel, who was meant to be the experience, elite manager to deliver success – not another disappointing lack of control when it really mattered.



But Tuchel is not about to step down or get sacked ahead of the home Euros in 2028.

The FA are backing their expensive hire to come good in two years.

It has now been revealed that Pep Guardiola had reached an agreement to take over the national team role in 2024.

He then went on to make a U-turn on his Manchester City future and England turned to Tuchel instead.

It was still seen as a giant coup – landing a manager as established and highly rated as this.



And all was going well – until the finish in Atlanta which has soured the feeling entirely.

Tuchel himself has expressed frustration at the English “DNA”, claiming that the nation’s history is simply not there – only making things worse with supporters.

An exclusive SunSport poll revealed that nearly 60 per cent of voters – out of 15,000 – felt he should be AXED.

Just 32 per cent thought Tuchel should keep his job, and high profile pundits are also split on the future.



Michael Owen slammed the former Chelsea man, labelling the approach as “rubbish” and like a “pub team.”

Gary Lineker was left unimpressed with the tactics and joked about Tuchel being a “German Spy.”

Fans watching a Tuchel interview laying into performances under Gareth Southgate have been upset by his own lack of invention and bravery on the biggest stage.

Even Lionel Messi felt England “didn’t want it” when Argentina turned up the heat.

Tuchel, 52, was appointed as Southgate’s permanent successor in late 2024 – starting on January 1, 2025 – and signed an extension until after Euro 2028.



That tournament is due to be played in England – but the initial goal was for Tuchel to deliver a second ever World Cup title and a second star on the shirt.

Now he has failed with that – and the manner in which it all turned ugly – has left questions over Tuchel’s position.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The FA will carry out a regular review of the tournament – which had mostly been a success until it all spiralled away in one half hour blitz.

Tuchel is expected to remain in charge. And making a change now will be extremely costly with none of the contract clauses triggered.

Sports.title: Jarrod Bowen agrees revised West Ham contract as Hammers risk losing host of key stars ahead of new Championship season
Sports.content:
JARROD BOWEN will stay at West Ham in the Championship after agreeing a new deal with the club.

The Hammers captain, a target for Everton and Chelsea over the summer, met with Czech owner Daniel Kretinsky in Prague and was convinced to stay at the London Stadium despite relegation.



Bowen, 29, has agreed new terms, though his deal is not thought to have been extended beyond the existing length of 2030.

West Ham have already sold Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham in an £85million deal, with Crysencio Summerville already expected to depart.



Kretinsky, whose influence has grown following David Sullivan’s resignation, was determined to keep his skipper at the club.

Bowen said: “The main motivation is staying and bringing this club back into the Premier League where we belong.

“It hurt everyone and it should hurt everyone, it was such a disappointing thing that happened. You can’t change it, it doesn’t last forever.

“I flew to Prague in the Czech Republic to meet Daniel and Jiri to go out and speak and the ambition I got from Daniel and Jiri, the direction the club wants to move in it interested me a lot. It didn’t take a lot for me because this club means a lot to me.

“I’ve been here six-and-a-half-years and transitioned from a boy from the Championship to a man and captain to the club, which is a huge honour.

“I see myself in years to come as a diehard West Ham fan so I always think what would they want as a fan if they got the opportunity to play on the pitch?

“It is about what we create as a group, what environment we want to create. There is going to be a different pressure on us now and the most important thing is the desire, attitude and a winning mentality.

“It is good to be back at Rush Green ready to go. We’re moving in the right direction as a club, there is a lot of thinking time over the summer and a lot of things that go in your head but for me I look in years and years to come, what is going to bring me the most happiness? Sports.title: Three quarters of Brits will be watching sport this summer
Sports.content:
SUMMER OF SPORT Three quarters of Brits will be watching sport this summer

AS MANY as 75 per cent of Brits will be watching sport this summer, spending more than 21 hours in the pub – sipping 24 drinks and singing along to 23 songs or chants.

A study of 2,000 adults found of those tuning in, almost half will be watching the tennis (47 per cent) and more than a third the F1 (34 per cent).



Two thirds of adults into summer sport will head down to the pub to watch an average of nearly seven different events – spending more than three hours in their local each time.

An average of nearly four drinks will be purchased during each event, with fans expecting to part with £83.30 when visiting the pub to watch sport this summer.



The research was commissioned by VELO, which has pinpointed the towns where it will be easiest to get a seat in the pub to watch sport over the next few months.

According to its data, Doncaster is the place where people are most likely to get a seat, and in London, it is the City of Westminster for the win.

Alina Ustymenko a spokesperson for VELO said: “There’s nothing quite like watching sport with a crowd, whether it’s belting out a chant, celebrating a score with a high five or pretending you know the rules of F1.

“The research shows fans are really throwing themselves into a summer of sport, with pubs set to be packed with fans, songs, snacks and hopefully enough seats to go around.



“Getting there early to claim your seat is going to be key ahead of some of the biggest sporting events of the summer.”

The study also found that simply wanting to watch with friends, family, or other fans is the top reason 51 per cent of pub goers head to their local to watch a game.

But 49 per cent like the better atmosphere and 45 per cent claim it feels like more of an occasion.

Others like the bigger screens (30 per cent) and having more food and drink options (18 per cent).

In fact, 76 per cent said watching sport with others at their local turns a match into a shared occasion.



When choosing a pub to watch a sporting event, 50 per cent look for one with a good atmosphere, while 48 per cent prioritise a big screen and a clear view.

While 31 per cent will opt for one with plenty of seating to ensure they have somewhere to sit down.

With pub goers arriving an average of 31 minutes before the start of a match or game to ensure they get a seat.

But when it comes to celebrating, 37 per cent of all adults, polled via OnePoll, have lost their voice from cheering or singing at a sporting event, while 32 per cent celebrate by jumping up and down.

Others sing or chant (27 per cent), share high-fives with others (18 per cent) or even hug those nearby (15 per cent).



Alina Ustymenko, added: “What really stands out is just how much excitement there is for a proper summer of sport down the pub.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Turning up early to bag a decent seat, knowing exactly what snacks they will be grabbing and getting ready to cheer on their teams, its clear fans are treating these matches like a real occasion.

“Whether they’re shouting at the screen, joining in with chants or just soaking up the atmosphere, the pub remains a huge part of how people enjoy sport together.”

Sports.title: Former European semi-finalists SHUT DOWN and forced to hand over keys to 28,000-capacity stadium after 123 years
Sports.content:
FORMER Portuguese champions Boavista have been forced to shut down after 123 years in a devastating blow for one of the country’s most historic football clubs.

According to Portuguese outlet A Bola, the club has been ordered to cease all operations after failing to meet financial obligations during insolvency proceedings.



Boavista have also been instructed to hand over the keys to the 28,000-capacity Estadio do Bessa, along with the surrounding facilities, by July 31.

The club must vacate the stadium “free of people and belongings” after insolvency administrators concluded there was no realistic prospect of the required funds being paid.



Boavista had been required to make monthly payments to cover current running costs and the deficits across the club’s various sporting departments.

However, those payments were not made – thus triggering the closure of all activities at the stadium and its adjacent facilities.



The club’s remaining sporting sections will only be allowed to continue operating until the end of July before the site is formally abandoned.

Clarisse Barros, the insolvency administrator, thanked Boavista’s directors, staff and coaches for their “grand, almost limitless dedication” during the club’s final months.

The collapse marks the end of one of Portugal‘s oldest football institutions, with Boavista founded in 1903.

They remain one of only five clubs to have won the Portuguese top flight, famously lifting the Primeira Liga title in 2000/01 to break the traditional dominance of Benfica, FC Porto and Sporting Lisbon – the only club in the last 80 years to do do.

Boavista also enjoyed memorable success in Europe.

They reached the 2002/03 UEFA Cup semi-finals, where they were edged out 2-1 on aggregate by Celtic.

The Scottish giants then returned to Seville for the final, only to lose 3-2 after extra-time to Jose Mourinho‘s Porto in a thriller of a game.

Financial problems have plagued Boavista in recent years, with the club placed into liquidation before registering its senior men’s side in Portugal’s fourth-tier district league last summer.



The team, however, failed to play a single competitive match, with the financial crisis continuing to spiral.

Now, one of Portuguese football’s most famous clubs will close its doors, bringing a sad end to a remarkable 123-year story.

Sports.title: World Cup winners to be given Super Bowl-style RINGS for first time ever as fans fume USA should ‘never host again’
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL fans are raging after it was revealed that the winners of the World Cup will be handed Super Bowl-style championship rings.

Fans have already been up in arms at the hydration breaks being used for extra advertising slots and the extended half-time show set for the final on Sunday.



But now the erosion of traditions has taken another step further with the awarding of rings for the first time in the World Cup.

Fifa announced that 30 members of the victorious team in the final showdown between France and Argentina would be given one of 2,026 rings created to commemorate this year’s tournament.



Predictably, Fifa also said the remaining 1,996 would be made available to fans worldwide as an “Official Licensed Product,” in what many fans view as yet another cash-grab.

This takes the World Cup final into new territory with the game already at the mercy of a rumoured 30 minute half-time show, ignoring the rules of the game that preclude the interval exceeding 15 minutes.



Announcing the new rings, Fifa said: “In addition to the iconic trophy and prestigious gold medals, a new symbol of triumph will be awarded to the winning team.

“In a momentous first for a Fifa competition, the tournament winners will also receive bespoke championship rings, bringing one of the most recognisable American sporting traditions to the global game.

“Each ring will be part of a strictly limited edition of just 2,026 individually numbered pieces, a direct tribute to the tournament itself.

“Of these, 30 will be presented to the victorious team, while 1,996 will be made available to fans worldwide as an Official Licensed Product, allowing supporters to own a unique piece of Fifa World Cup 2026 history.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“One side of the ring proudly features the Fifa World Cup trophy, while the other will be customised to reflect the identity of the winning team. Each ring will be individually numbered, custom-fitted and delivered with its own certificate of authenticity.

“Immediately after the final, the captain and head coach of the winning team will receive temporary rings to commemorate the occasion.

“Each of the 30 rings for the winners will then be customised before being officially presented at a later date, ensuring the perfect lifelong fit for an achievement that will echo through eternity.”

Rings are, of course, a long-standing tradition in the NFL, NBA and MLB.



They have handed to the winners of the Super Bowl, NBA Finals and World Series for many decades and feature ornate designs with customised engravings and jewels for the winning team.

But many football fans feel this is a step too far from Fifa.

One X user said: “Understand that the World Cup is happening in the USA, but we do not have to Americanise the sport. This isn’t Football.

“We don’t flex rings, We flex medals. I speak for everyone when I say we do not want this. No one wants this s***.”



Another commented: “The bastardisation of this tournament has been unbelievable. What next? Time outs and free kicks sponsored by some weak as p*** Yank beer?”

A third posted: “A reminder that the rings, the half-time show, the drinks breaks are all FIFA initiatives which they’ve been wanting to do for a long time, and have done them in America because they know everyone will blame America and not Fifa.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A fourth noted: “The US should never be allowed to host again.”

England will take on France in the third-place play-off on Saturday before Argentina and Spain meet for the biggest prize in the game – and some rings.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland finally responds to Tom Holland’s request after Norway’s World Cup hero ‘humbled’ Hollywood star
Sports.content:
ERLING Haaland has finally responded to Tom Holland’s dinner request after “humbling” the Hollywood A-lister.

Holland, 30, revealed on Jimmy Fallon this week that he’d sent the soccer star a DM, only to be blanked.



Having spotted Haaland at an F1 race in Monaco, the Star Wars actor decided to ping him an invite to dinner.

“That is exactly the type of humbling experience that is important for actors,” Holland told Fallon on The Tonight Show.



“You know, you’ll be like, ‘I’ll text him, I’ll take him to dinner.’

“[There was] not even a response, not an excuse, not ‘I’m busy tonight, I’m playing football,’ Nada.

“I was watching Lewis Hamilton race, and I saw him.

“He was in a hospitality suite across from me, and I just thought I’d shoot my shot. Send him a text.

“I never imagined I would talk about it on live television, but here we are.”

The Tonight Show went on to post a clip of Holland telling the story to Instagram, with the upload receiving more than two million likes.



And among those to see the video was Haaland himself.

Sports.title: Falklands banner held by shameless Argentina stars was smuggled in fan’s sweaty UNDERWEAR – and could appear in final
Sports.content:
THE Falklands banner paraded by shameless Argentinian players after knocking England out was smuggled into the stadium hidden in a fan’s sweaty underwear.

The defending World Cup champions sparked fury for waving a vulgar sign claiming “The Falklands are Argentinian” after beating England 2-1 in Wednesday’s semi-final.



And the footballers reportedly kept the disgraceful sign for themselves after the game, prompting fears they could whip it out again at Sunday’s final.

The flag was taken back to Argentina‘s team hotel – and could fly to New York with them.



Patricio Auber, a waiter who has accompanied the squad to the States, posted photos posing with the banner at the team hotel on Instagram.

He smirked in the snap with the offensive flag, writing: “To whom it may concern. It’s in good hands.”



Players held the huge sign that falsely claims “The Falklands Islands are Argentinian” after a fan threw it down to the field.

The fan who smuggled the sign into the Atlanta stadium – despite bans on political banners – has bragged about how he made it from a hotel bedsheet and a £7 pot of paint.

He boasted to Todo Noticias: “I folded it as much as I could, put it in my private parts to get through security checks, and in the end we managed to get in.



“When I saw Montiel, I threw it to him and he caught it. He passed it to Lo Celso, who was the first to hold it up.”

“When I saw Lo Celso unfold it and his teammates holding it on the field, I felt a joy that I can’t put into words.



“How a piece of a bedsheet could mean so much to all Argentinians.”

The flag-smuggler, reportedly from Villa Luro, Buenos Aires, admitted he hadn’t acted alone, saying “we made it on the same day as the match”.

Seeking to shirk responsibility and shift blame to his own supporters yesterday, defender Gonzalo Montiel insisted: “They just threw one down from the stands and the boys grabbed it.”

Argentina’s madcap president has even backed up the team and boasted that they’ll probably only receive a fine for their pathetic behaviour.

Nationalist firebrand Javier Milei spewed: “It is perfectly valid and legitimate for the players to want to express themselves and do so.”



The Falklands Islands’ own government has even slammed the crass banner.

They said: “The Falklands government is disappointed – though regrettably not surprised – that the Argentine football team decided to tarnish the result of last night’s World Cup football semi-final – a game that did not in any case involve the Falkland Islands.

“That said, it is hardly news to anyone that the people of the Islands were victims of an aggressive invasion in 1982, which left many traumatised.”

Downing Street has backed calls for Argentina to be hit with some form of punishment from Fifa for the abhorrent display.

Under Fifa’s disciplinary code, political gestures of this nature usually result in financial penalties rather than sporting sanctions.



The Argentine Football Association (AFA) will most likely face a hefty fine, alongside a formal warning about future conduct.

A statement from No10 on the controversy read: “The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are.”

The islands in the south Atlantic are a British territory that the UK fought a bitter war to defend in 1982, when Argentina’s military dictatorship launched a brutal invasion.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They are home to a population of around 3,500 who voted almost unanimously to remain British in 2013, but Argentina can’t let the grudge go and still claims the territory for themselves.

Britain have claimed the islands since before the state of Argentina declared independence from its coloniser Spain in 1816.

Sports.title: Harry Kane's 'irritating' behaviour annoys referee as England get brutal truth
Sports.content:
Harry Kane's 'irritating' behaviour annoys referee as England get brutal truth

England were beaten 2-1 to Argentina and Harry Kane has been criticised by a former Premier League referee

View 2 Images Harry Kane has been criticised (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Former Premier League referee Graham Scott has criticised the ‘irritating’ behaviour from England star Harry Kane during their World Cup defeat to Argentina. The Three Lions lost 2-1 to get knocked out of the tournament in the semi-final stage, and will now face France in the third-place play-off.

‌



England had held a 1-0 lead thanks to a second-half goal from Anthony Gordon, before Argentina responded with goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez to secure the victory.

‌



Referee Ismael Elfath handed out four yellow cards across the 90 minutes, with just one going to an England player. Lisandro Martinez, Cristian Romero and Rodrigo De Paul were all booked for Argentina, while Elliot Anderson was cautioned for England.

‌



Scott, who spent 10 years refereeing in the Premier League, explained why he did not like what he saw from the England players during the defeat to Argentina.

England dressing room was left raging after star swapped shirts with Argentina rival READ MORE :

"It really annoys me watching our players trying to chip away at the ref because that's not going to work," Scott told talkSPORT. "I've been on the receiving end of it from these people.

"It just annoys you [as a referee]. It doesn't get you what you want [as a player]. It doesn't achieve what you're hoping it will achieve.

‌



"And, well, the Argentinians seem rather more effective at it – so what can we learn from that?

"It's also understanding about how different referees operate. So, do we actually watch the ref? Do we analyse them before the game? Do we think, 'Right, he's going to let this go'?

View 2 Images Harry Kane of England (Image: Julian Finney - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌

"We [referees] can exploit that as well, potentially, but also, be ready for that onslaught because it's coming."

Scott also opened up on what it’s like to referee a game with Kane and offered some advance for the England captain.

‌



"He's [Kane] very repetitive," Scott said. "And it is the sarcastic leading question of 'Is he going to be allowed to do that all day? Are you going to give us anything? Do you know there are two teams out here...?'. And it just irritates you.

"[I used to think], 'I wish you'd just go away' and then... if anything, when the 50-50 call comes in, 'No, you're not getting it, because I've taken against you as a person now'.

Sports.title: How England could line up at Euro 2028 as harsh Harry Kane reality is exposed
Sports.content:
How England could line up at Euro 2028 as harsh Harry Kane reality is exposed

England's World Cup dreams were ended by Argentina on Wednesday night, with Thomas Tuchel now set to turn his attentions to the European Championship in two years

View 4 Images Thomas Tuchel and Harry Kane

Thomas Tuchel still has the chance to lead England to their best-ever World Cup on foreign soil.

‌



For all the disappointment and frustration of the surrender to Argentina, it was only England’s fourth semi final. They lifted the trophy in 1966, lost amid the tears of Turin in 1990 and again to Croatia in the 2018 World Cup.

‌



The third place play-off is the game nobody really wants and England lost to Italy in 1990 and to Belgium eight years ago.

‌



Now, if they beat France and finish third in the tournament - far from an easy task - then it will still be seen as even more of an overwhelming success by those in power at the Football Association.

And beyond that, England have what can loosely be called a home Euros in 2028 when Tuchel really will be expected to deliver. After losing back-to-back Euro finals under Gareth Southgate, Tuchel was hired to get England over the line and to finally become winners.

They just missed out on a place in the World Cup final but, when Tuchel signed a new two-year contract extension, he referenced how much managing England in the Euros would mean to him.

‌



That is why Tuchel will be certain to look at the next generation for Euro 2028 and, in particular, who can break into what will be his next England team.

This World Cup has been very much a mixed bag for Jordan Pickford thanks to heroics against Mexico but also the England keeper being questioned over Enzo Fernandez’s equaliser for Argentina, an erratic display against Croatia and some nervous kicking.

It feels as if Pickford could come under serious pressure for the first time since he was made No1 ahead of the 2018 World Cup.

‌



View 4 Images Jordan Pickford's place could come under threat moving forward

That should come in the form of Manchester City ’s James Trafford who recognised during this tournament that he will need to be No1 somewhere to realistically challenge Pickford which is his ultimate goal.

Trafford has long been seen at the FA as a natural long-term successor as No1 keeper but that went wrong after his move to City last summer because his arrival was quickly followed by Gianluigi Donnarumma. If Trafford can get regular Premier League game time, then this could be his big chance.

‌



At right back, Reece James is a Tuchel favourite but his injury record has opened the door. Trent Alexander-Arnold is not his cup of tea but Ben White and Tino Livramento are pushing through.

Marc Guehi is set in stone in central defence and really it is the flanks where competition looks to be heating up. If Myles Lewis-Skelly keeps up his progress, then he will surely be back into the squad sooner rather than later after his remarkable end to the season.

Arsenal ’s teenage prodigy Max Dowman can play as a No10, deeper in midfield but also wide right and he is really one to watch.

‌



Dowman was out in New York during the World Cup for an Adidas shoot and next time he could be starring on the pitch rather than off it. Dowman is destined for the very top but is still only 16 so maybe he will not be starting for England until the next World Cup.

The same goes for Alex Scott because the Bournemouth midfielder definitely has a big chance of he keeps progressing after being called up to the England training group in Florida ahead of the World Cup.

View 4 Images Rio Ngumoha could be a key part of England's attack by 2028

‌



The other player is Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha who was another called up to the pre-camp in Florida and his future looks incredibly bright. Ngumoha is very much an attacking force from the left and we saw glimpses of his potential in the friendly against New Zealand.

But this World Cup ended up being a success for Anthony Gordon and you have to balance the attacking mentality of Ngumoha against the defensive responsibilities of Gordon.

Either way, there is real strength and quality there. And that is not something you can say about the centre forward position.

‌



The harsh reality is there is no-one ready to step into Harry Kane ’s boots. He turns 33 later this month, he will be 36 at the next World Cup and even the Euros will be a stretch at 34.

There is simply no-one. Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney are both 30, they barely got a look-in this time and yet Dom Solanke, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Liam Delap have not grasped the mettle.

Eddie Nketiah was once a big hope but never kicked on. England have such an issue that Tuchel identified Phil Foden and Cole Palmer as being able to play false nines. Neither even made this squad.

‌



England have talent in abundance - but not up front.

View 4 Images How England could line up at the Euros in 2028

England's possible Xi for Euro 2028: James Trafford; Tino Livramento, Marc Guehi, Levi Colwill, Myles Lewis-Skelly; Declan Rice, Elliot Anderson; Bukayo Saka, Jude Bellingham, Rio Ngumoha; Harry Kane.

Arsenal have already been busy in the transfer market, with both incoming and outgoing deals having been completed and Mikel Arteta is now aiming to add to the Gunners’ youth ranks again

View 2 Images Arsenal have already been busy in the transfer market (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal are showing ‘strong interest’ in a deal for Cardiff City youngster Axel Donczew in what could be another eye-catching swoop.

‌



The Gunners have already been active in the market this summer, with a series of deals having been completed. Piero Hincapie has been signed on a permanent deal following his loan spell, while Ilian Meslier has added to the North Londoners’ goalkeeping ranks.

‌



On the outgoing front, Leandro Trossard has departed for Besiktas, with Jakub Kiwior having joined Porto on a permanent deal.

‌



Arsenal could rubber-stamp another significant move over the coming days, with a deal having been agreed for Club Brugge’s Christos Tzolis. But it now appears that the Gunners are also keen to add to their youth ranks, too.

As per The Telegraph, Arsenal have strong interest in Cardiff midfielder Donczew, who broke the Welsh club’s record of their youngest-ever player last season after making his debut at 15 years and 234 days.

Arsenal talks on next transfer 'advanced' after Christos Tzolis deal agreed READ MORE :

Speaking at the time, Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy said: "I think it's probably a bit surreal for them in this moment, but you can see from their families it's an extraordinarily powerful occasion for them.

Sports.title: Who was really to blame for England's World Cup exit: Thomas Tuchel or the players? Have your say
Sports.content:
In the end, the semi-final was the limit.

From the outset, not just of the tournament but ever since Thomas Tuchel was hired to replace Gareth Southgate, England's World Cup ambitions have been crystal clear: Win the bloody thing.

The former Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain boss was, initially, handed a big-money 18-month contract where the sole focus was on winning the World Cup, 60 years on from the Three Lions solitary triumph. And while the FA and Tuchel extended their agreement pre-tournament to take in Euro 2028 too, the goal this summer remained the same.

England World Cup player ratings: Bellingham shines but Arsenal duo suffer after gruelling season READ MORE :

‌



But when it came to the crunch, the real crunch - we're not talking second round struggles against DR Congo or last 16 trips to the Azteca - England, as has so often been the case in recent years, were found wanting. For Croatia 2018, Italy 2021, France 2022 and Spain 2024, add Argentina 2026. Once again, when they found themselves facing a team to whom they were widely considered either equal or slightly inferior to, it was the end of the road.

Since the defeat in Atlanta, there has been no shortage of criticism, much of it pointed at Tuchel and his substitutions. After all, he took the decision to go ultra defensive with his changes.

But is it all down to the manager? What of the players, who at 1-0 elected to stop pressing high and started dropping deeper, ceding possession and retreating to the edge of their 18-yard box BEFORE any subs were made?

"When we went 1-0 up we seemed to try and hold on, which at this level is not enough," admitted Harry Kane. At 1-0 up, footage shows Tuchel and his No.2, Anthony Barry, instructing players to push forwards - while subs on the sidelines tell the XI on the field to drop back.

‌



So what do you think? Was Tuchel the biggest reason for England's semi-final demise? Was it the players who ultimately couldn't do what was required? Or does fault lie somewhere in between?

Sports.title: Falkland Islands government launch plea to FIFA in telling response over Argentina banner
Sports.content:
Falkland Islands government launch plea to FIFA in telling response over Argentina banner

A number of Lionel Scaloni's players brandished a controversial banner reading 'The Falklands are Argentinian' in the aftermath of their nation's 2-1 win over England in the World Cup semi-finals

View Image Argentina players held up a banner in the aftermath of Wednesday's match (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

The Falkland Islands' Government has urged FIFA to sanction the Argentinian football team after dragging politics into sport at the World Cup. A number of Lionel Scaloni's players held up a banner reading 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas' in the aftermath of the nation's 2-1 World Cup semi-final win on Wednesday evening.

‌



That message translates to 'The Falklands are Argentinian' in a bitter jab over the the ownership of the South Atlantic islands. While Great Britain colonised the Falklands in 1833, Argentina invaded the nation in 1982, sparking a 74-day war which saw more than 100 warships deployed by then-Prime Minister, Margaret Thatcher.

‌



As a result of the conflict, 649 Argentinian military personnel, 255 British armed forces and three Falklands civilians died, with England defending their land. However, Argentina have continued to dispute the sovereignty, with a belief that they have the rights to their neighbouring islands.

‌



OPINION FIFA have got the World Cup final they always wanted after painful England exit by John Cross

That ultimately prompted a showing of protest from the Argentina national team on Wednesday, with players bringing political matters into football - something which has been considered a no-no by FIFA for some time.

Official regulations from World Football read: "For any offence the player and/or the team will be sanctioned by the competition organiser, national football association or by FIFA."

‌



And now, the Falkland Islands Government has urged FIFA to stick to their word, calling for sanctions for the Argentine team for their actions. In a statement, they told Mirror Football: "The Falkland Islands Government is disappointed – though regrettably not surprised - that the Argentine football team decided to tarnish the result of last night’s World Cup football semi-final - a game that did not in any case involve the Falkland Islands.

"That said, it is hardly news to anyone that the people of the Islands were victims of an aggressive invasion in 1982, which left many traumatised. The banner displayed by Argentina last night, therefore, was particularly insensitive for many people in the Falklands.

"It is the avowed policy of the Falkland Islands Government that we do not wish to see politics being brought into sport. Nor do we wish the Islands and their people to be used as a political football in every conversation about England and Argentina.

‌

"We welcome the UK Government’s supportive statement this morning. As Business Secretary Peter Kyle highlighted, the World Cup has as one of its central tenets that politics is separate from football.

‌



"We hope FIFA will make good on their promise to keep politics out of sport, and sanction all behaviour of this nature in line with its own rules."

It comes after Kyle also called for similar sanctions. He said: "My reaction is that it was entirely inappropriate. Politics needs to be separate from football.

"In fact, the World Cup has one of its central tenets that politics is separate from football. That is now a matter for FIFA. I expect FIFA to do its investigation thoroughly."

‌



He added: "I think it was certain to happen because it was such an egregious violation of the rules of not having political activity as part of the football."

FIFA have since released their own statement on matters, with a spokesperson saying: "As is standard procedure, FIFA's independent disciplinary committee is currently assessing the match reports and considering the relevant circumstances before deciding on potential further steps based on the FIFA disciplinary code."

Sports.title: Pep's prediction correct as Rodri returns to dominant best
Sports.content:
Rodri came in for some criticism in Spain after they were held to a goalless draw by Cape Verde in their first game of the World Cup. There were accusations that he had moved the ball too slowly; that he was in some way responsible for the result.

His manager made it clear he felt otherwise. "It seems incredibly insulting to me that people would say that about the best player in the world," said Luis de la Fuente. "Would people say that about others who are considered the best? I don't think they would dare.

"But because he's Spanish, we say things about our own that we wouldn't about others. Rodri is the best player in the world. Even at 50 per cent, he is better than most other midfielders. He brings clarity, vision, balance. Rodri is an inspiration for us."

Five weeks and six straight wins later, it is easy to forget how this tournament began for Spain and their captain, whose performances on their run to the final have proved his manager right. If not the best in the world, then certainly the best in his position.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on The Rest is Football, Gary Lineker and John Obi Mikel were left seriously impressed by Rodri's performance against France in the World Cup semi-final

He came into it on the back of a difficult season domestically following his return from the anterior cruciate ligament injury suffered in the previous campaign as setbacks hindered his efforts to recapture his best form. But it has all played out exactly as Pep Guardiola predicted for the 30-year-old in October.

"I said to him, and he maybe struggled to understand, it's not about six, seven, eight months out, then playing and being the Rodri of before. No. Do you know when Rodri will be good? At the World Cup with Spain. At the World Cup he will be the best Rodri."

Spain's strength lies in the collective. Their semi-final victory against star-studded France highlighted the value of teamwork over individuals. But it certainly helps to have this version of Rodri bringing it all together in the centre of the pitch.

He heads into Sunday's final against Argentina having completed the most passes by any player at a World Cup on record, with 655. He has helped Spain grind opponents down by circulating the ball, while also offering speed and incision when required.

His total of 62 line-breaking passes in the final third is the most by any player at a World Cup since Toni Kroos hit the same number for Germany on their way to winning it in 2014. Only winger Alex Baena has created more chances among Spain players.

At a tournament in which Spain have averaged 64 per cent possession, almost everything has travelled through him. Rodri has had roughly 20 per cent more touches and made roughly 20 per cent more passes than any player from any side.

"Every time you see him, he's always showing up for the ball," said the former Chelsea midfielder John Obi Mikel on The Rest Is Football. "It doesn't matter whether he makes a mistake, he's always available."

His willingness to take responsibility is part of his role as their leader and he has demonstrated his excellence off the ball as well as on it. His ability to read danger and put out fires has helped Spain restrict their opponents to a solitary goal in seven games.

Rodri has made the second-most tackles at the tournament. He also ranks highly for possessions won in the middle and final thirds. France actually had a roughly even share of possession in Tuesday's semi-final but Rodri dominated all phases of play, winning 11 out of 15 duels, including four out of four aerials.

All of it has been underpinned by a level of professionalism that has helped him navigate a challenging return from injury and play 627 minutes of a possible 630 at the tournament.

Those who have worked with him say his unerring commitment to his preparation has been apparent since his youth.

"He stood out for his intelligence as a footballer, but also because he was also very clear about how a young player should behave," Paco Lopez, his coach in Villarreal's B team, told Sky Sports. "A lot of boys can get distracted, but he always understood what was required to become a professional."

Rodri still has that knack for understanding what is required, on the pitch as well as off it. He effectively plays the role of a second coach, organising his team-mates in and out of possession and dictating the tempo as he has for Spain throughout the tournament.

Image: Rodri and Mikel Merino leap with joy after Spain's last-gasp winner against Belgium

His return to top form comes at a time of some uncertainty around his future. Rodri only has a year remaining on his contract at Manchester City. In signing Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m, they appear to have secured a long-term successor.

On the evidence of the last five weeks, though, and the performances that have put him and his country one more win away from lifting the World Cup, Rodri continues to set the standard.

Sports.title: Bowen commits future to West Ham despite relegation
Sports.content:
Jarrod Bowen has committed his future to West Ham despite their relegation from the Premier League.

There were doubts over whether Bowen would stay at the club for their first season in the Championship since 2012, with midfielder Mateus Fernandes having already left for Tottenham in an £85m move and winger Crysencio Summerville wanted by Manchester United, among others.

Bowen joined West Ham from Hull City in a £22m deal in January 2020 and signed a new seven-year contract in October 2023 - and he is determined to win promotion with West Ham back to the Premier League.

"The main motivation for me is staying and bringing this club back into the Premier League where we belong," the forward said.

More to follow.

Sports.title: Shields ready to continue talks for Price super fight
Sports.content:
Claressa Shields is ready to resume talks for a women's super fight against Lauren Price.

Shields appeared in Cardiff for a face-off with Price in April, stoking up expectation that a fight could be finalised between America's multi-weight world champion and the unified welterweight title holder from Wales.

The fight is yet to be confirmed and Shields is currently preparing for a middleweight fight against Kaye Scott for the WBC and WBA titles on August 15, but her promoter Dmitriy Salita is hopeful that a deal can be agreed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lauren Price has said she would 'love to share the ring' with Claressa Shields

"When Claressa went to Wales, we believed we had the framework of a deal in place, and we're still operating in that spirit," Salita told Sky Sports.

"I believe we're close. Claressa is moving down to 160lbs because she wants to make this fight happen. She's already accomplished so much but she's always looking for the biggest global fights.

"She wants to face the best fighters and continue helping women's boxing reach new audiences around the world.

"Lauren is an outstanding fighter and an Olympic gold medallist. This is one of the biggest fights that can be made in women's boxing and we're confident it will happen.

"Claressa has always done her part to make the biggest fights possible and this is no different. We're ready to continue the discussions."

"She has the opportunity to do something that's only been accomplished once in more than 100 years - move down from heavyweight and win the middleweight world title.

"That's where all of her attention is. Once that challenge is behind her, she'll continue pursuing the biggest fights available, and Lauren Price is certainly one of them.

"Absolutely, we'd love to make the fight. Throughout Claressa's career, we've worked with promoters from every major company because we believe the best fighters should face each other.

"That's how the sport grows, that's what the fans want, and that's the approach we've always taken. We're willing to work with everyone to make the biggest fights in women's boxing happen."

Sports.title: England vs Argentina: A one-sided rugby rivalry - will Pumas bite back?
Sports.content:
Fresh from the drama of Wednesday's FIFA World Cup semi-final between England and Argentina, the nations meet again on Saturday as part of rugby's Nations Championship in Santiago del Estero.

While the history of England vs Argentina in football has been punctuated by huge moments and massive victories on both sides, the rugby history between the English and the Pumas is rather different.

Ahead of meeting on Argentine soil this Saturday, the two sides have met in 30 previous Tests dating back to 1981, and England's dominance is near stark.

The record reads 24 England victories, five Argentina wins and one draw.

The Pumas have steadily grown as a side over the decades, sensationally reaching the semi-finals of the Rugby World Cup in 2015, and picking up marquee wins over New Zealand in 2020, 2022, 2024 and 2025, and South Africa in 2015, 2016, 2018 and 2024 - beating both home and away. They've also beaten Australia four times since 2022.

Yet, for all Argentina's impressive success on a world stage, England have continued to prove something of a bogey team.

Image: While Argentina have picked up sensational victories over New Zealand and South Africa in recent years, England have proven a bogey side

The sides have met five times at World Cups, and England have won every meeting: Pool stage conquests in 1995, 2011, 2019 and 2023, plus a third-place play-off in 2023 only Argentina will know how they lost.

England toured Argentina in 2025, 2017 and 2013 when missing a host of British and Irish Lions players selected the same summers, and even still won each series 2-0, securing victories in all six Tests.

Argentina wins have come in 1990, 1997 and 2009 on home soil, and in 2006 and 2022 at Twickenham, but successes have been few and far between.

Indeed, England have won the last five meetings in a row and 15 of the last 16 Tests between the sides.

In 14 meetings in Argentina, England have won 10 and Argentina three, plus a draw in 1981. In England, the hosts have won nine from 11 Tests to Argentina's two wins.

Image: England vs Argentina contests in rugby have routinely proven feisty affairs, but England have come out the victors more often than not

Image: Argentina's one-point victory over England at Twickenham in 2022 is their only success in the last 16 meetings between the sides since 2009

So, is this 2026 Test the occasion Argentina turn up and give their best against England?

While October saw a very unfortunate, narrow defeat to the might of South Africa, and November stirring wins over Wales and Scotland - the latter victory from 21 points down with 24 minutes to play - Argentina's most-recent performances have not been good.

They were totally outplayed by Scotland two weeks ago in a 47-38 defeat on home soil in Cordoba, while they shipped 21 points to a Wales side struggling for wins over the last number of years in an eventual 35-21 win in San Juan last week.

England were on a run of five Test defeats in a row before last weekend's heavy victory over 14-player Fiji, following a brutal fifth-place Six Nations finish and thumping defeat in South Africa a fortnight ago, but their tails are now up.

Image: England halted a run of five straight Test defeats with a thumping win over Fiji last week

Amid everything else, there is also the small matter of the context around November's England vs Argentina meeting to factor in on Saturday.

Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi labelled England flanker Tom Curry a "bully" and claimed to have been "smacked" by the player in the tunnel following England's 27-23 win that day.

Nothing further came of the spicy incident, but you can be sure Argentina and Contepomi haven't forgotten.

Image: Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi called England flanker Tom Curry a 'bully' and claimed to have been 'smacked' by him in November

Freeman: We're expecting 'angry' Argentina atmosphere and Pumas side

The England squad and set-up, who were based in Buenos Aires until Thursday before heading north to Santiago del Estero, took the decision not to wear national shirts when in Argentina, in light of the tension surrounding Wednesday's fixture.

Wing Tommy Freeman, when speaking to media this week, added he expected an even angrier atmosphere and opposition than is customary for the England rugby side in South America.

"We'll see how hostile it gets here," Freeman said. "It's big for Argentina and us and being here it's heightened massively.

Image: England wing Tommy Freeman says the squad are preparing for an 'angry' atmosphere and contest vs the Pumas on Saturday

"I think they'll probably be angry, so Saturday could be a tough game.

"We know they're a passionate country. We are too and they'll want to compete to the fullest and we'll be ready for that."

England second row Alex Coles added: "I think, bearing in mind where we are and who we're playing with, we've been pretty sensible about not wearing our English shirts around too much."

Pepper: Pumas fans have football-crowd mentality but we can 'shut them up'

England back-row Guy Pepper was also speaking to the media earlier this week, and while conceding he expected an increased football-crowd type energy for the Test, has backed his team-mates to "shut up" the locals.

Pepper has played two Tests in Argentina before now, in La Plata and San Juan last year as he made his Test debut. A replacement in both matches, the 23-year-old says he was able to appreciate and feel the passion Argentina fans bring.

"It was very much football-crowd type mentality out there, which was cool to experience and different," Pepper said.

"It was noisy, but you were also able to shut them up by outscoring them. It was a real rollercoaster of emotion.

Image: England have picked up 2-0 series wins in Argentina in 2013, 2017 and 2025 despite the absence of British and Irish Lions players each tour

"Being on the bench for the two games, you could take in the fact that they're all chanting and jumping around one minute and then you can hear a pin drop the next.

"On reflection, the 2025 Argentina tour was quite significant for this group, particularly with the Lions guys being away.

"It was a pretty cool and special moment for us, an important step to breed new young players and allow them to make a name for themselves and keep the jersey. It was a pretty special tour and something that will only make us tighter.

"Since that tour we have really tried to step up the way we attack games, so that we are able to play through teams and also play around them. It's exciting where we're going."

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Arapaho Gold chases Newbury hat-trick
Sports.content:
Newbury and Wolverhampton are the venues for Friday's live action on Sky Sports Racing.

4.10 Newbury - Arapaho Gold, Nabati and Social Symbol clash

The Listed Apple Print & Creative Rose Bowl Stakes is a belter with unbeaten pair Nabati and Arapaho Gold headlining 12 runners.

Charlie Appleby took this prize last season with subsequent Middle Park winner Wise Approach and Nabati has strong claims under William Buick. He oozed class when justifying skinny odds to make an impressive debut at Yarmouth and it will be fascinating to see if he can build on that in the Godolphin blue.

Arapaho Gold is the principal danger for Michael Dods and Connor Beasley. He has two victories from as many starts to his name after a pair of easy Thirsk outings and deserves a crack at this higher grade.

Social Symbol stepped up on his debut to claim fourth in the Norfolk Stakes and a repeat of that form would see him hit the frame with Ryan Moore a notable booking. This lad is a full-brother to Royal Spa, who was only a few lengths behind the great Thorpedo Anna at her peak.

Another to note is Windsor Castle fifth Sale Shark, while God Given Talent may bounce back after his Ascot disappointment in the Michael Buckley colours. This will be trainer James Ferguson's final runner before he pursues pastures new.

3.00 Newbury - Well-bred Force Of Light among 15 runners

A plethora of well-bred two-year-olds head to post for the Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes, where Force Of Light makes most appeal.

Appleby's son of Lope De Vega is a brother to dual Group One scorer Shadow Of Light and has Earthlight among other top-class relatives in his pedigree. He is drawn in stall 11 and all eyes will be on this Godolphin newcomer.

Cilician represents Brian Meehan and brings in the most experience having had three starts to date. Second on his debut, he finished down the field at the Royal meeting but another runner-up effort at Sandown has seen him given a rating of 90 - that might see him in the mix.

Plenty can be monitored in the market, with Shoot You Down and Arthurian a couple for the shortlist.

4.28 Wolverhampton - Go Rimbaud and Chapter lock horns

A small but select field has assembled for the Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Handicap at Dunstall Park.

Go Rimbaud landed his first success on his fourth outing at Kempton back in April (form franked) before disappointing when favourite for a handicap at Haydock later that month. He returns from a break having undergone a gelding operation and remains capable of better.

Chapter recovered from a lesser effort to score at Sandown last month and can go well if the blinkers continue to work.

Brocklesby Bill - named in honour of the late Bill Turner - and On The Inlet complete the field.

Best of the rest

Newbury's BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (3.35pm) sees plenty of powerful ownership groups represented. Cheveley Park's Lady Of Hay is of interest, being a son of St Mark's Basilica out of a Group Two-placed dam. Faith In Florence ran a respectable fourth on debut at Yarmouth and could put that experience to good use here.

Later on the card (5.20pm), Green Sky bids for a hat-trick in the Uhy Ross Brooke Fillies' Handicap but last-time-out winner Kelly Burn is a danger.

1h ago 06.13 EDT The pitch where Spain forward Lamine Yamal honed his skills ⁠in a working-class, multi-ethnic neighbourhood outside Barcelona was buzzing with life on Thursday as locals looked ahead ⁠with pride to ⁠the World ​Cup final against Lionel Messi’s Argentina. “Now that the moment has come when the two of them are ⁠going to play against each other, it’s incredible,” said Keba, an 18-year-old Senegalese resident, referring to Barcelona forward Lamine ⁠Yamal’s well-known admiration for Messi. Messi, 39, enjoyed the peak years of his ​career at Barcelona having come through ‌the club’s youth ‌academy and a viral photograph showing the Argentine with a baby Lamine ‌Yamal, now 19, has captured imaginations ahead of Sunday’s final in New Jersey. View image in fullscreen A football court in Rocafonda. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters As children from migrant families played on a pitch behind a mural featuring Lamine Yamal’s face in the Rocafonda neighbourhood, in the coastal city of Mataro, his grandmother, Fatima Nasraoui, and his 15-year-old ‌cousin Rayan watched from a nearby bench. “I want Spain to win,” she said, adding that she would shout loudly ​if he scores. “To me, Lamine means many good things, but above all he’s like a brother because we grew up together,” his cousin said. Lamine Yamal, who was born in Spain to a Moroccan father and mother from ⁠Equatorial Guinea, has never forgotten his roots. Throughout his career, ​he has honoured ​Rocafonda with his trademark “304” hand ​gesture after scoring goals - a reference to the neighbourhood’s ​postal code. During the ‌World Cup, he ​has worn ​a headband with “Rocafonda” on it, donned the flags of his parents’ countries of origin on his boots, and said football was an example of racial and social integration. Reuters View image in fullscreen A man walks past a graffiti depicting Lamine Yamal in Rocafonda. Photograph: Josep Lago/AFP/Getty Images Share

3h ago 04.18 EDT Trent Alexander-Arnold said it is “a pleasure” to work with reappointed Real Madrid ⁠manager Jose Mourinho, adding that he has long admired the Portuguese coach and believes he can ⁠help the club ⁠win trophies. Mourinho ​returned to Real Madrid in June for a second spell after a disappointing campaign last ⁠season in which they missed out on the LaLiga title and were eliminated from the Champions League quarter-finals. “I ⁠have always admired the coach (Mourinho). I’ve played against him a couple ​of times, and it’s ‌a pleasure to work ‌with him and his team,” Alexander-Arnold said. “It’s ‌intense. The principles and the level of demand are very high, so I’m looking forward to seeing how, the more we get to know each other, the more we learn and the more he can teach us. And we’re all willing ‌and eager to learn and improve. I’m sure he’ll teach us many things and help us win trophies this ​year.“ Alexander-Arnold, who joined Real Madrid from Liverpool last year, endured an injury-hit first season in Spain and did not always command a regular place in the starting line-up, rotating in and out ⁠of the side. However, the departure of defender Dani Carvajal in ​May has ​opened an opportunity for Alexander-Arnold ​to establish himself as Madrid’s first-choice right-back. “I’ve been ​out of action ‌for a long ​time, so ​it’s good to finally be back and to lay a solid foundation for a successful season,” the 27-year-old Englishman added. Reuters View image in fullscreen Trent Alexander-Arnold in pre-season training. Photograph: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid/Getty Images Share

3h ago 04.11 EDT James Moriarty writes: “The thing that is really bothering me, in this endless Brave England’s failure autopsy, is this - Tuchel was, until the semi-final, universally praised for making game changing substitutions. Which is all well and good, but it happened seemingly in every game, which surely points to a bigger issue: namely that NONE of his starting line-ups worked, and games were only won by substitutes changing the course of the match. England were staggeringly lucky to get as far as they did, and were the worst of the semi-finalists by a country mile, so perhaps we should all be grateful that Tommy T has spared the embarrassment of getting humbled by Spain in the final.

Anyway, I’m very much looking forward to France Reserves vs Jordan Henderson XI tomorrow.” I would argue in the world of five substitutions that there is always a plan to throw the ‘finishers’ on. I think the subs against Norway were rather odd, to be honest, too. Share

3h ago 04.08 EDT Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez will attend the World Cup final to see his country take on reigning champions Argentina, his government said Friday. Sports.title: More than 200 countries endorse Infantino for fourth Fifa term despite Balogun scandal
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has the formal endorsement of more than 200 countries for re-election as Fifa’s president despite the climate of unrest that has swirled since the scandal surrounding Folarin Balogun’s reprieve from suspension.

The Guardian understands only a handful of Fifa’s 211 member associations are still to send letters of support for Infantino, who is on course to be voted into a fourth term by a landslide at its congress in March. A small number of European countries are among the outliers, with Germany the highest-profile FA yet to provide official backing.

Candidates must be put forward by 18 November, before which time letters can also be withdrawn or transferred to a different contender. But Infantino is currently the only runner and some FAs feel they have, nonetheless, come under persistent pressure from within Fifa to confirm their allegiance. In theory that should not be permitted under Fifa’s ethics code.

It would take a political earthquake to dislodge Infantino. Although there remains disquiet after Donald Trump admitted lobbying Fifa to review the USA striker Balogun’s red card against Bosnia and Herzegovina, the vast majority of it is festering among European FAs and adjacent bodies. Infantino does not need to count on Europe’s support to land an overwhelming mandate and, in any case, most of the continent has confirmed its endorsement for his re-election. The English FA is among those to have sent its letter well in advance of the World Cup.

The topic of a Europe-backed candidate to run against Infantino has gained legitimacy behind closed doors over the past 10 days but the prospect of multiple federations settling upon a name feels remote.

Uefa has made its opposition to Fifa clear on a number of recent issues, such as the Balogun incident and the barring of the Somali referee Omar Artan from the World Cup, but it is unclear whether the governing body’s leadership would feel moved to support formally a contender for the election. Some sources close to European football’s hierarchy feel a candidate who could amass 30 or 40 votes would at least be able to open a legitimate public debate about Fifa’s governance and direction of travel.

Fifa’s member associations will convene in New York on Saturday although, with Infantino helming the meeting, the subject of recent scandals is unlikely to be an agenda item. The World Cup’s financial performance, and any subsequent benefits that could be passed on to the FAs, is more likely to be a topic of discussion.
